TX-01.why: TX-01 is an ACH debit by Brightwave Telecom she never agreed to (no access device lost); it is on the August statement sent 2 September, so the 60 days run to 1 November and she is liable for nothing; she gets back 186 dollars

TX-04.why: TX-04 is an online purchase with a copied number, before the card was lost on 28 September (M-1); no access device was lost at the time, it is on the September statement sent 2 October, so she is liable for nothing; she gets back 412.60

TX-11.why: TX-11 is a 400 dollar ATM withdrawal with the card lost on 28 September; she learned on 29 September and told the bank on 30 September (M-1), inside two business days, so she is liable for 50 and gets back 350

TX-12.why: TX-12 is a 95 dollar top-up made on a new device with a code read out to a caller (A-3, A-4, A-5, comment 2(m)-3); she learned on Wednesday 7 October (M-2, A-5), and today, Friday 9 October, is the second business day, so she is liable for the lesser of 50 and 95, which is 50, and gets back 45

traps.TX-07: TX-07 is 1,200 dollars she sent herself from her usual phone (A-2) to a scammer; a transfer she starts is authorised, however she was persuaded (rules, authorised)
traps.TX-08: TX-08 is 150 dollars of fuel her son Teo bought with the card she let him use (M-4); authorised until she tells the bank otherwise
traps.TX-09: TX-09 is 89 dollars she spent herself and returned; the merchant has promised the refund by 14 October (M-3), so there is no error
traps.TX-10: TX-10 is a 64.99 dollar purchase already refunded on 3 October (TX-14)
traps.TX-13: TX-13 is the 15.99 dollars a month for Tidewatch Plus that she signed up for on 3 January (M-5); she authorised it
traps.TX-03: TX-03 is the same subscription, 15.99 dollars on 1 September, which she authorised (M-5)
traps.TX-05: TX-05 is already the subject of claim C-1; it is chased, not reported again
traps.TX-06: TX-06 is already the subject of claim C-3, which the bank has credited
traps.TX-15: TX-15 is already the subject of claim C-2, filed on 7 October
traps.CC-1: CC-1 is a credit card charge at Cardhollow; it is not a transfer from her bank account and falls under Regulation Z, not Regulation E

C-1.why: C-1 was filed on 18 September; the bank's 10 business days ended on 2 October with no answer and no provisional credit (claims list), so it is late and she asks for the 318.40 dollar credit

traps.C-2: C-2 was filed on 7 October and the bank has until 22 October; it is not late
traps.C-3: C-3 has been credited 129 dollars on 1 October, inside its 10 business days; there is nothing to ask for
